The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: Commons describes it as Arianus of Antinoe, prefect of Egypt, martyred with companions at Antinoe under Diocletian, in the Menologion of Basil II. Antinoe stands in the Thebaid, this folder's place, and the converted prefect is the only Arianus the calendar keeps. Commons describes it: Arianus of Antinoe. Prefect of Egypt, martyred with companions at Antinoe in Egypt under Diocletian. Arianus and a co-martyr, sewn into sacks, are thrown into the sea. In the sea, dolphins carry the bodies of three co-martyrs, in sacks, toward the shore. Константинополь. 985 г. Миниатюра Минология Василия II.  Ватиканская библиотека. Рим.
